questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a solitary, firm, non‑tender mass in the right upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined lesion within the liver. Which histological feature is most characteristic of hepatocellular carcinoma?
options: A. Presence of fibrous septa and pseudoglandular structures
B. Sheets of pleomorphic cells with prominent nucleoli
D. Spindle cells with storiform pattern
questions.explanation: HCC shows sheets of pleomorphic cells with prominent nucleoli; fibrous septa are seen in cholangiocarcinoma, mucin in adenocarcinoma, spindle cells in sarcoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common site of origin for metastatic breast cancer to the bone?
questions.explanation: The thoracic and lumbar spine is the most frequent site of bone metastases from breast cancer; other sites are less common.

questions.stem: A 60‑year‑old woman has a 2‑cm ulcerated lesion on the lower lip. Histology shows nests of atypical epithelial cells with keratin pearl formation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Keratin pearls are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma; basal cell carcinoma shows palisading, melanoma shows melanin, adenocarcinoma shows gland formation.

questions.stem: Which of the following immunohistochemical stains is most useful for confirming a diagnosis of metastatic melanoma?
questions.explanation: S100 is a sensitive marker for melanoma; cytokeratin stains epithelial cells, CD20 B‑cell, desmin muscle.

questions.stem: A 35‑year‑old man has a 3‑cm mass in the left adrenal gland. Histology shows nests of cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and a “Zellballen” pattern. Which hormone is most likely overproduced?
questions.explanation: Pheochromocytoma shows Zellballen nests and secretes catecholamines; cortisol/aldosterone are from cortical tumors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a well‑differentiated liposarcoma?
options: C. Fibrous septa with spindle cells
questions.explanation: Lipoblasts with multivacuolated cytoplasm are hallmark of liposarcoma; high mitoses, fibrous septa, necrosis are more typical of high‑grade sarcomas.

questions.stem: A 70‑year‑old woman presents with painless jaundice. Imaging reveals a 4‑cm mass in the head of the pancreas. Histology shows irregular glands lined by atypical epithelial cells with mucin production. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma shows irregular glands with mucin; neuroendocrine tumors are neuroendocrine, acinar cells produce enzymes, mucinous cystic neoplasms are cystic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common histological type of colorectal carcinoma?
questions.explanation: Conventional adenocarcinoma accounts for >90% of colorectal cancers; mucinous and signet ring are rarer, lymphoma is non‑epithelial.

questions.stem: A 50‑year‑old man has a 2‑cm ulcerated lesion on the tongue. Histology shows a proliferation of spindle‑shaped cells with a storiform pattern and inflammatory infiltrate. Which diagnosis is most likely?
options: B. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
questions.explanation: Kaposi sarcoma shows spindle cells in a storiform pattern with vascular slits; other sarcomas have different patterns or lack vascular features.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a classic histological feature of Crohn’s disease?
questions.explanation: Crohn’s disease often shows non‑caseating granulomas; crypt abscesses are typical of ulcerative colitis, villous blunting in celiac, pseudopolyps in UC.

questions.stem: A 55‑year‑old woman has a 3‑cm mass in the left ovary. Histology shows sheets of cells with abundant clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Which immunohistochemical marker is most useful for confirming a diagnosis of clear cell carcinoma?
questions.explanation: HNF1β is strongly expressed in clear cell carcinoma of ovary; ER/CA125 are more general, p53 is mutated in many carcinomas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common type of primary bone tumor in adults?
questions.explanation: Chondrosarcoma is the most common primary bone malignancy in adults; osteosarcoma and Ewing are more common in children, giant cell tumor is benign.

questions.stem: A 30‑year‑old man presents with a painless, firm mass in the scrotum. Histology shows nests of malignant cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Which tumor is most likely?
questions.explanation: Testicular carcinoma from seminiferous tubules shows malignant nests with eosinophilic cytoplasm; seminoma is uniform, Leydig and Sertoli are sex cord‑stromal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic histological feature of a well‑differentiated thyroid carcinoma?
options: A. Papillary nuclei with nuclear grooves
B. Follicular cells forming true papillae
questions.explanation: Papillary carcinoma shows nuclear grooves and clearing; follicular cells form true papillae in papillary, Hurthle cells in follicular, anaplastic shows pleomorphism.

questions.stem: A 55‑year‑old man presents with a solitary, firm, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑circumscribed lesion arising from the spleen. Which of the following histological features is most characteristic of a benign splenic hemangioma?
options: Blood-filled vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells
Acral fibroblastic proliferation with collagen deposition
questions.explanation: Benign splenic hemangiomas consist of dilated vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells. The other options describe features of sarcoma, adenocarcinoma, and fibrous tissue, respectively.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common cause of acute pancreatitis in adults?
questions.explanation: Gallstones are the leading cause of acute pancreatitis in adults, followed by alcohol abuse. Hypertriglyceridemia and autoimmune pancreatitis are less common.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old woman has a 2‑cm, submucosal mass in the sigmoid colon. Histology shows a well‑demarcated lesion composed of spindle cells arranged in a whorled pattern. Which immunohistochemical stain is most likely to be positive?
questions.explanation: Gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GISTs) are CD34 positive. S100 indicates neural crest tumors, cytokeratin indicates epithelial origin, and desmin indicates muscle differentiation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the histological appearance of a well‑differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon?
options: Solid sheets of pleomorphic cells with necrosis
Glandular structures lined by tall columnar cells with mucin vacuoles
Sheets of small blue cells with scant cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Well‑differentiated colonic adenocarcinoma forms glandular structures with mucin production. The other patterns describe squamous, sarcomatous, and neuroendocrine tumors.

questions.stem: A 60‑year‑old man has a 3‑cm mass in the right hepatic lobe. Biopsy shows sheets of polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and a fibrous capsule. Which tumor type does this most likely represent?
questions.explanation: The described morphology is classic for hepatocellular carcinoma. Focal nodular hyperplasia and adenoma are benign, while hemangioma shows vascular channels.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a malignant melanoma?
options: Spindle cell proliferation with collagen deposition
Pigmented nests of atypical melanocytes in the epidermis
Well‑demarcated, non‑encapsulated lesion of uniform cells
questions.explanation: Malignant melanoma shows pigmented nests of atypical melanocytes in the epidermis and dermis. The other options describe sarcoma, adenocarcinoma, and benign neoplasm.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of a pancreatic pseudocyst?
options: Excessive excretion of pancreatic enzymes into the peritoneum
Collection of pancreatic fluid encapsulated by fibrous tissue
Formation of a true cyst lined by epithelium
questions.explanation: A pseudocyst is a collection of pancreatic fluid surrounded by a fibrous wall, lacking epithelial lining. The other options describe necrosis, leakage, and true cysts.

questions.stem: A 50‑year‑old patient has a 4‑cm mass in the left adrenal gland. Histology shows a well‑circumscribed tumor composed of cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and a characteristic “salt and pepper” chromatin pattern. Which hormone is most likely overproduced?
questions.explanation: The described morphology is typical of an adrenocortical carcinoma producing cortisol. The other hormones are associated with different adrenal tumors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a hallmark of a well‑differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus?
options: Spindle cell proliferation with collagen deposition
Sheets of small blue cells with scant cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Keratin pearls and intercellular bridges are classic features of squamous cell carcinoma. The other patterns describe adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, and neuroendocrine tumor.

questions.stem: A 70‑year‑old woman presents with a 2‑cm mass in the left kidney. Histology shows a well‑circumscribed lesion composed of cells with clear cytoplasm and a delicate capillary network. Which tumor type does this most likely represent?
options: Renal cell carcinoma, clear cell type
questions.explanation: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma shows clear cytoplasm and a rich capillary network. Oncocytoma has eosinophilic cells, angiomyolipoma has fat, and papillary carcinoma has papillary architecture.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the histological appearance of a typical benign lipoma?
options: Well‑demarcated lobules of mature adipocytes surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule
questions.explanation: Benign lipomas are composed of mature adipocytes in well‑demarcated lobules with a fibrous capsule. The other options describe sarcoma, adenocarcinoma, and fibrous tumors.

questions.stem: A 65‑year‑old man has a 3‑cm mass in the pancreas. Histology shows a well‑defined lesion composed of nests of epithelial cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and a fibrous stroma. Which tumor type is most likely?
questions.explanation: Neuroendocrine tumors form nests of epithelial cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm. The other options describe adenocarcinoma, cystadenoma, and acinar carcinoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a malignant fibrous histiocytoma?
options: Spindle cells arranged in a storiform pattern
Sheets of small blue cells with scant cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma (undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma) shows spindle cells in a storiform pattern. The other options describe benign lipoma, adenocarcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumor.

questions.stem: A 55‑year‑old woman has a 2‑cm mass in the ovary. Histology shows a cystic lesion lined by a single layer of cuboidal epithelium with abundant glycogen. Which type of cyst is this most likely?
questions.explanation: Serous cystadenomas are lined by cuboidal epithelium rich in glycogen. Mucinous cystadenomas have columnar mucinous epithelium, endometriomas are lined by endometrial tissue, and dermoids contain ectodermal elements.

questions.stem: A 55‑year‑old man presents with painless jaundice and weight loss. Imaging shows a mass in the head of the pancreas. Which histologic feature is most characteristic of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma?
options: Glandular structures lined by tall columnar epithelium with mucin production
Desmoplastic stromal reaction with irregular glands in a fibrotic background
Well‑differentiated squamous epithelium forming keratin pearls
questions.explanation: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma shows a desmoplastic stroma with irregular glands; mucinous glands are typical of mucinous cystic neoplasms, neuroendocrine tumors have granules, and squamous epithelium indicates squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.stem: A biopsy of a 3‑cm breast lesion shows a proliferation of pleomorphic cells with prominent nucleoli and frequent mitoses. Immunohistochemistry is positive for GATA3 and ER. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: ER and GATA3 positivity with pleomorphic cells indicates invasive ductal carcinoma; lobular carcinoma shows discohesive cells, phyllodes is biphasic, and fibroadenoma is benign.

questions.stem: A 60‑year‑old woman has a 2‑cm mass in the left ovary. Histology reveals solid nests of cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Which marker is most useful for confirming the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: WT1 is a sensitive marker for serous ovarian carcinoma; CK7 is non‑specific, calretinin is mesothelial, and CD10 is endometrial stromal sarcoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common cause of acute pancreatitis in the United States?
questions.explanation: Gallstones are responsible for ~40–50% of cases; alcohol is second, hypertriglyceridemia and autoimmune are rarer.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man has a 4‑cm ulcerated lesion on the lower lip. Histology shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifacts. Which immunostain would best confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: HMB‑45 is positive in melanoma; S100 is less specific, CK5/6 is squamous, CD117 is GIST.

questions.stem: A 70‑year‑old man presents with a large, firm, non‑tender mass in the right upper quadrant. Imaging shows a 10‑cm hepatic lesion with central scar. Which histologic finding would confirm the diagnosis of hepatic adenoma?
options: Fibrous septa with bile duct proliferation
Fatty change and glycogen accumulation in hepatocytes
Hyalinized central scar surrounded by fibrous tissue
questions.explanation: Hepatic adenoma shows fatty change and glycogen in hepatocytes; fibrous septa and bile ducts are cirrhosis, spindle cells are fibrolamellar carcinoma, and hyalinized scar is focal nodular hyperplasia.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic histologic feature of malignant melanoma?
options: Nests of atypical melanocytes with prominent nucleoli
questions.explanation: Melanoma shows nests of atypical melanocytes; Reed–Sternberg cells are Hodgkin lymphoma, spindle cells are sarcomas, keratin pearls are squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 35‑year‑old woman has a 1‑cm skin nodule on the forearm. Histology shows a well‑circumscribed lesion composed of bland spindle cells arranged in a whorled pattern. Which immunostain is most diagnostic?
questions.explanation: CD34 is positive in dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans; S100 is neural, desmin is muscle, AE1/AE3 is epithelial.

questions.stem: A 50‑year‑old man has a 3‑cm ulcerated lesion on the tongue. Histology shows a proliferation of pleomorphic cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and a prominent nucleolus. Which marker would confirm the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma?
questions.explanation: p63 is a marker for squamous differentiation; HMB‑45 is melanoma, S100 is neural, CDX2 is intestinal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common histologic type of lung cancer in smokers?
questions.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is most common in smokers; adenocarcinoma is most common overall, small cell and large cell are less frequent.

questions.stem: A 60‑year‑old man presents with a 2‑cm mass in the right adrenal gland. Histology shows sheets of cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Which immunostain would best confirm adrenal cortical carcinoma?
questions.explanation: Melan‑A (MART‑1) is a marker for adrenal cortical cells; synaptophysin and chromogranin are neuroendocrine, cytokeratin is epithelial.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old woman has a 5‑cm mass in the left kidney. Histology shows a mixture of epithelial and stromal components with a prominent fibrous stroma. Which diagnosis is most likely?
options: Renal cell carcinoma, clear cell type
Renal oncocytic neoplasm with fibrous stroma
questions.explanation: Renal oncocytic neoplasm with fibrous stroma (oncocytoma) shows epithelial and stromal components; clear cell RCC is vascular, angiomyolipoma has fat, and oncocytoma lacks fibrous stroma.
